plan_a_advantages: More targeted intensity work (tempo run, strength sessions) to improve speed.
Two longer runs at moderate effort, better simulating trail running demands.
plan_b_advantages: Greater emphasis on building a solid aerobic base with longer, easier runs.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates more targeted, higher-intensity work while prioritizing recovery. While Plan B focuses heavily on building aerobic base with longer, easier runs, Plan A includes a tempo run and more frequent strength sessions, both crucial for improving speed and efficiency on trails. The inclusion of two longer runs at moderate effort also allows for better adaptation to the demands of trail running, which often involves sustained effort over varied terrain. Plan B’s emphasis on consistent easy running is valuable, but it lacks the specific stimuli needed to translate into faster times.
